The US needs to add, on average, about 145,000 new jobs per month just to keep unemployment levels from rising. I don't think this is due to a lack of desire. Behind the scenes Trump is probably promising them incentives that will make keeping/adding factories in the US cost equivalent to outsourcing them, but manufacturing automation has jumped by leaps and bounds. And 2,000 people of today can do the jobs of tens of thousands of the past. And even reducing the population does nothing to fix this. It's the ratios that change. Before you needed let's say 1,000 people to help manufacture the cars for 100,000 other people. Now you might only need 100 or even 50 people to manufacture for the same population. On average worker productivity has increased by about 500% across all sectors since the fifties, so a 1000% increase in productivity in manufacturing would hardly be surprising. The point is that if you decrease the population and you decrease the number of workers needed. It's the proportions that are changing. We live in a society where everybody, who isn't already well off, needs a job to make ends meet - yet the number and proportion of jobs required to produce everything for society continues to decline.

BOSTON – Senator John Kerry, with his mother’s New England patrician pedigree and his Irish last name actually has a grandfather who was born a Jew in the former Austro-Hungarian Empire.

The news was a revelation to Kerry himself, who only found out about his Jewish roots while running in the 2004 presidential election.
